decisive_spans.text: a firm, globular 6×4 cm mass within the vaginal canal
a separate cervical os could not be identified
the uterine fundus was not palpable

response.rationale: The presence of a mass in the vaginal canal, an unidentifiable cervical os, and an unpalpable uterine fundus strongly suggest uterovaginal prolapse. While uterine leiomyoma is a possibility, the description of the mass and the inability to palpate the uterus or identify the cervix point more directly to prolapse.
